<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right"><B>Exhibit 99.1 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Atrium Therapeutics Announces FDA Clearance of Investigational New Drug </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Application for ATR 1072 for Treatment of PRKAG2 Syndrome </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; ATR 1072 is the company&#8217;s first precision cardiology program to enter the clinic -- </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> will be the first clinical trial for people living with PRKAG2
syndrome that evaluates a potential treatment for the underlying cause of the disease &#8212; </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">SAN DIEGO, July&nbsp;14, 2026 /<U>PRNewswire</U>/
&#8212; Atrium Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RNA) (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to delivering RNA therapeutics to the heart, announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared its
Investigational New Drug (IND) application allowing the Company to move forward with its <U>Corventis</U><U><SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP></U><U> Phase 1/2 clinical tria</U>l designed to evaluate ATR 1072 for the
treatment of Protein Kinase <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-catalytic</FONT> subunit Gamma 2 (PRKAG2) syndrome. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;PRKAG2 syndrome and other rare genetic cardiomyopathies represent a profound unmet need &#8212; these are progressive, life-altering and
life-threatening diseases that often strike early, affect multiple members of the same family, and have no approved therapy to address their root cause,&#8221; said Kathleen Gallagher, President and Chief Executive Officer, Atrium Therapeutics.
&#8220;FDA clearance of our IND and the launch of the Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> Phase 1/2 trial reinforce our team&#8217;s ability to move with speed on behalf of patients with the goal of delivering
potential disease-modifying treatments.&#8221; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> is a Phase 1/2 open-label,
multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of ATR 1072. The study will enroll approximately 37 participants across two parts: Part A, multiple ascending dose cohorts to
characterize safety and support dose selection, and Part B, a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">single-arm</FONT> expansion cohort at the recommended Phase 2 dose to further evaluate safety and efficacy trends in cardiac structure and function. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Clinical site initiation activities are currently underway, and Atrium expects the first participant to be enrolled by the end of 2026. Initial trial data
demonstrating proof of concept is anticipated in the second half of 2027. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About ATR 1072 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">ATR 1072, the company&#8217;s lead product candidate, is a potentially disease-modifying treatment for PRKAG2 syndrome. Using Atrium&#8217;s precision RNA
delivery technology, ATR 1072 uses small interfering RNA (siRNA) to silence mutant PRKAG2 messenger RNA (mRNA), normalize <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> protein kinase (AMPK) activity and reduce pathogenic glycogen
accumulation, potentially leading to improved heart function. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About PRKAG2 Syndrome </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare, autosomal dominant, early-onset cardiomyopathy caused by mutations in the PRKAG2 gene, which encodes the Gamma 2 regulatory subunit
of AMPK. Mutations enhance AMPK activity leading to abnormal glycogen accumulation in the heart, thickened heart muscles, electrical conduction problems, and arrhythmias. Based on current scientific literature estimates, there are at least 1,000
&#8211; 2,000 people with PRKAG2 syndrome in the US. Current management is limited to symptomatic treatment; no approved therapies exist to address the underlying genetic driver of disease. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About the Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> Trial </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> is a Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety,
tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of ATR 1072 in participants living with PRKAG2 syndrome. The study will enroll approximately 37 participants across two parts: Part A, multiple ascending dose cohorts to characterize
safety and support dose selection, and Part B, a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">single-arm</FONT> expansion cohort at the recommended Phase 2 dose to further evaluate efficacy trends in cardiac structure and function. Additional information about
the trial is available at <U>www.corventistrial.com</U>. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About Atrium Therapeutics </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Atrium Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RNA) is pioneering targeted delivery of ribonucleic acid (RNA) therapeutics to the heart to transform the standard of care
for people living with cardiomyopathies. The Company&#8217;s proprietary technology&#8212;designed at Avidity Biosciences, Inc.&#8212;combines the tissue selectivity of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and other targeted delivery ligands with the
precision of oligonucleotides. Atrium Therapeutics&#8217; platform is designed to selectively target the underlying drivers of genetically driven cardiac diseases through targeted, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-viral</FONT> delivery of small
interfering RNA (siRNA). This approach builds upon learnings from demonstrated delivery to the skeletal muscle and applies it for efficient delivery to the heart with the potential to overcome challenges associated with <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-specific</FONT> tissue delivery. The Company&#8217;s pipeline consists of two precision cardiology candidates, ATR 1072 for PRKAG2 (Protein Kinase <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-catalytic</FONT> subunit Gamma 2) syndrome and ATR 1086 for PLN (phospholamban) cardiomyopathy, and two undisclosed research targets in rare cardiomyopathies. </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
